title: Introduction to N-d Array and its Creation

blocks.content: Course: Python Numpy for Data Science
Introduction to N-d Array and its Creation
NumPy is not restricted to 1-D arrays, it can have arrays of multiple dimensions, such arrays are also known as N-dimensional arrays or ndarrays.
An array can have any number of dimensions and each dimension can have any number of elements.
For example, a 2D array represents a table with rows and columns, while a 3D array represents a cube with width, height, and depth.
How to create a N-d array?
Creating an N-dimensional array is similar to creating a 1-dimensional array. Instead of passing a 1-D list, we provide an N-d list to the np.array() function.

# create 2D array
array1 = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])

# create 3D array
array2 = np.array([[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]])

items: array1 is a 2D array created using np.array() by passing a nested list of values as an argument.
array2 is a 3D array created using np.array(), but this time with a nested list structure that represents multiple matrices.
